WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Cancellation of Licences of Foreign Fishing Vessels 
*281. SHRI CO. POULOSE: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are considering to cancel the licences issued to the 
foreign fishing vessles; 
(b) if so, by when; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI NITISH KUMAR): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) Does not arise. 
(c) There are no foreign fishing vessles opera ting in Indian waters at present. 
However, as per earlier deep sea fishing po licies, foreign vessels were under operation 
till October, 2000, all of which have since been repatriated after expiry of their permits. 
Wages of Female Workers 
*282. MISS MABEL REBELLO: 
SHRIMATI     SAROJ             DUBEY: 
Will the Minister of LABOUR be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware of the fact that female workers are paid 
4 

[15 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
less than their male counterparts in most of the unorganised sectors in the 
country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and 
(c) whether Government intend to equalise wages of male and female workers, 
if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR (DR. SATYANARAYAN JATTYA): (a) to (c) The 
Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 provides for payment of equal remuneration to women for the 
same work or work of similar nature. The Central Government is the appropriate Government 
in relation to any employment carried on by or under die authority of the Central 
Government or railway administration, or in relation to a banking company, a mine, oilfield 
or major port, or any corporation established by or under a Cental Government Act. In respect 
of all other employments, the State Governments are the appropriate Governments. Under 
the Act, officers of the appropriate Government notified as Inspectors make inspections 
and prosecute those found violating provisi ons of the Act. The Central Government 
monitors the implementation of the Act.

Indians Arrested in Saudi Arabia 
* 286. SHRI S. RAMACHANDRAN PILLAI: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that over the last two years thirty Indians have been arrested 
on charges of illegal trafficking of narcotics in Saudi Arabia; 
(b) if so. the amount of punishment awarded to them; and 
(c) the number of Indians who have been granted mercy on approach by the Indian 
Government's Missions in Riyadh and Jeddah? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI J AS WANT SINGH): (a) and (b) 
Yes, Sir. Over the last two years, 30 Indians have been arrested and later executed in 
Saudi Arabia on charges of illegal trafficking in narcotics. 
(c) Saudi laws provide for capital puni shment for all crimes involving drug 
trafficking. Though the Indians Mission interacted with Saudi authorities for grant of mercy 
in such cases, these requests could not be acceded to on account of strict local laws. 
However, in respect of charges other than drug trafficking, 535 Indian prisoners were 
granted Royal amnesty during the year 1999-2000.

Flexibility in Hardware Sector 
*288. SHRI KARTAR SINGH DUGGAL: Will the Minister of 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to stale: 
(a) while India's performance in software has been commendable, what steps are 
being taken to make the le eway in hardware sector in so far as Information 
Technology is concerned; and 
(b) whether Singapore and Malaysia are far ahead of India and if so, what steps are 
contemplated to nourish it in order to enable it to do reasonably well in hardware sector 
on the line of software sector? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI PRAMOD 
MAHAJAN): (a) and (b) Steps taken for the developmcnl of IT Sector as a whole are as 
under:— 
1. Export Promotion Capital Goods scheme (EPCG) has been rationalised and 
extended uniformly to all sectors wilhout any threshold limit on payment of 
5% duty. 
2. Approvals for all foreign direct investment proposals relating lo the 
Information Technology sector, with the exception of Business-to-consumer 
(B2C) e-commerce are under the automatic route. 
3. Powers of approval of the Designated Officers of MIT for 
8 

[15 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
implementation of STP and EHTP schemes have been further enhanced up to 
US$20 million. 
4. Accelerated depreciation norms for computers and computer 
peripherals for units u nder Export Oriented schemes (EOU/ EPZ/STP/ 
EHTP) have been enhanced. These shall stand depreciated to overall 
limit of 90% over a period of 3 years instead of around 5 years earlier. The 
Depreciation on Computers has been allowed @60%. 
5. DTA access upto 50% of the FOB value of export is permitted for software 
units under EQU/STP schemes, and fo r electronics hardware units under 
EOU/EPZ/EHTP schemes. Broadbanding is permitted in the DTA sales of 
Hardware units for items covered in the Letter of Permission, 
6. Special Economic Zones are being set up to enable hassle free 
manufacturing and trading for export purposes. 
7. Value addition norms for Rupee exports to Russiareduced from 100% to 33% 
under Advance Licensing Scheme. 
8. In the Budget 2001-02, the peak rate of customs duty continues @ 35%. 
Customs duty surcharge @ 10% has been abolished on all imports, in general 
but Special Additional Duty (SAD) @ 4% continues on all imports, except 
specific exemptions, In the 2000-01 Budget, Customs duty on Computers 
and Peripherals had been reduced from 20% to 15% and continues to be 
same. The Customs duty on all storage devices, integrated circuits, 
microprocessors, data display tubes and deflection components of colour 
monitors also continues at 0%. In the 2001-02 Budget, Customs duty on 
Information Technolgoy Agreement (ITA-1) items of WTO (IT and 
Telecom products) has been reduced from existing 20—25% to 15%. The 
concessional rate of customs duty for specified raw materials for the 
electronics industry continues. 
9. In the Budget 2001-02, the Central Excise duty structure has been 
rationalised from multiple rates to single rate of 16% and single rate of Special 
Excise Duty (SED) @ 16%. 
1 0 .  Information Technology Software  is exempted from Customs and 
Excise Duty.

Committees to Deal with Natural Calamities and Disaster 
Management Programmes 
2090. SHRI KRISHNA KUMAR BIRLA: Will the Minister of 
AGRICULTURE he pleased to slate: 
(a) what are the various committees set up by Government to deal with natural 
calamities and disaster management programmes; 
(b) the composition and function of each of such committees; 
(c) whether any review of the functioning of these committees has been made 
by Government in the light of the experience gained during the calamities and 
catastrophes caused by cyclones and earthquakes in the country; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the steps contemplated by Government  for the effective management in 
such situation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI 
SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK): (a) to (e) Institutiona l arrangements exist at the National. 
Slate and District levels for management of natura l disasters. The primary 
responsibility for undertaking rescue, relief and rehabilitation measures as well as 
disaster preparedness and mitigation programmes in the event of natural disasters is 
that of the State Government concerned.  The Central Governme nt supplements the 
efforts of the State Government by extending financial and logistic support. 
In the wake of the earthquake in Gujarat, a National Committee on Disaster 
Management has been set up under the Chai rmanship of the Prime Minister also 
having the representatives of the National and State Level Political Parties inter-alia 
to suggest necessary institutional and legislative measures needed for an effective and 
long-term strategy to deal with major natural disasters. 
The first meeting of the Committee was held on 18th Februray, 2001 and it was 
decided to constitute Working Group and Task Force for suggesting long term 
measures to deal with major natural disasters. 
A High Powered Committee on Disaster  Management has been set up in 
August. 1999 inter- alialo recommend measures for st rengthening organizational 
structures and comprehensive model plan fo r management of the disaster-both natural 
and manmade, at the National, State and District levels. The Committee has since 
submitted two interim reports.

AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:

AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI V. SREENIVASA 
PRASAD): (a) In order to boost export of s ugar, Government has taken the following 
measures:- 
(i) The sugar meant for export has been exempted from the levy obligation. This 
exemption which was initially available for a period of six months, commencing 
from 11th June, 2000, has been extended upto 31.3.200.

obligation the same may be availed by  the concerned sugar factory from the 
production in the 2000-2001 sugar season. 
(iv) DEPB at the rate 5% of the F.O.B. value of exports of sugar has been allowed. 
(v) APEDA have waived 5% performance Bank Guarantee to be furnished by the 
exporters.

to 30% with effect from 1.1.2000 and in order to achieve better targeting in supply of levy 
sugar under the Public Distribution System (PDS), the Government had excluded, with effect 
from 1.7.2000, the income tax assesses and members of their families from the purview of

further reduction in levy obligation of domestic sugar producers to 15% with effect from

increased, with effect from 1.2.2001, the minimum per capita supply of sugar to eligible 
persons under the PDS from 450gms to 500 gms.

AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRIV. SREENIVASA PRASAD): (a) and (b) No, Sir. 
(c) The Government of India had set up a High-Powered Committee on Sugar 
Industry headed by Shri B.B. Mahajan in March 1997. The Committee studied the 
entire gamut of the sugar economy and submitted its report in April 1998. The 
Committee has made a number of recommenda tions with a view to ensure healthy 
growth and development of the sugar industry and building a healthy relationship 
between the farmers and the sugar industry. The Government has recently taken decisions 
on all the recommendations of the Committee. 
The Government has taken die following measures to mitigate the problems of 
sugarcane growers as well as that of sugar industry:- 
(i) The Government has reduced levy  obligation on domestic producers from

MT of imported sugar. 
(iii) The Government has imposed levy obligations on importers of sugar at par with 
the domestic producers with effect from 17.2.2000. 
(iv) Stockholding limit on the recognized dealers has been removed w.e.f. 7.7.2000. 
(v) Sugar mills have been allowed w.e.f. 25.1.2000 to sell up to 10% of their monthly 
quota of freesale sugar by the 7th day of the succeeding month.

Disposal of foodgrains lying with FCI 
† 2149. DR. A.K. PATEL: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND 
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a huge stoc k of foodgrains has been lying in the 
godowns of the Food Corporation of India since last ten years and it could not be 
disposed off till the year 1999; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor, State-wise and the names of the foodgrains lying 
there alongwith the quantities thereof; and 
(c) what simple measures are contemplated by Government for the disposal of such 
foodgrains? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SRIRAM CHAUHAN): (a) The stocks of 
foodgrains available in the Central Pool with FCI and other procuring agencies depends 
on the production of foodgrains, their arrival in the Mandies, procurement under 
Minimum Support Price (MSP) operations and offtake from the Central Pool. With the 
upward revision in the MSP's of wheat and rice every year, the procurement has also been 
increasing. Stocks keep on increasing or decreasing depending upon the level of 
procurement of stocks during each crop season, and the quantity lifted against the 
allocation made for TPDS and other Welfare schemes of Government of India every 
month. 
(b) Statements I to IV, showing commodity -wise, stock-wise and category-wise 
postion of foodgrains available with FCI dur ing the last five years are enclosed. (See 
below). 
(c) For disposal of foodgrains, the following steps have been taken by the 
Government; 
(i) Open sale of wheat at reduced pric es has been started from 11.07.2000 and 
prices have been further reduced in  the East, West and South Zones in 
March, 2001; 
(ii) Open sale of rice has been started from 4.9.2000; 
(iii) The Central Issue Prices of wheat and rice were revised down wards 
from 25.7.2000; 
(iv) The CIPs of wheat and rice for the APL families have been fixed at 100% of 
the Economic cost or the open Market Sale prices decided by

per family per month is now being made on the basis of Population Projections of 
the Registrar General as on 1.3.2000 instead of projected population of 1995; 
(vi)   Foodgrains at BPL rates are available for allotment to State Governments per

Demand of Rice and Sugar 
2150. PROF. M.M. AGARWAL: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) the annual estimated demand of rice and sugar in the different parts of the 
country during the last 3 years; 
(b) the details of the actual allocation made by Government to the States 
during the above period; and 
(c) the steps taken by Government to increase the quantum of rice and 
sugar as per the demand of the States? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, 
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRISRIRAMCHAUHAN): (a) and (c) 
Allocation of foodgrains (wheat and rice) under Targeted Public Distribution System 
(TPDS) is based on average annual liftin g for the past ten years at the time of 
introduction of TPDS. Allocation of foodgrains to States/ UTs for BPL families was fixed 
so as to provide 10 kg. foodgrains per BPL family per month at specially subsidised rates 
on the basis of the poverty estimates given by the expert group appointed by the 
Planning Commission, Transitory allocation of foodgrains for families above poverty line 
(APL) was made equal to the difference between past 10 years' average annual lifting of 
foodgrains under PDS and the BPL entitlement. The bifurcation of foodgrains quota into 
rice and wheat both for APL and BPL categories was left to the choice of States/UTs. 
From April, 2000, the allocation of foodgrains (rice and wheat) to the States/UTs 
under TPDS for BPL families has been doubled from 10 kg. to 20 kg. per family per 
month. However, APL allocation to all Stat es/UTs has been maintained at the same 
level as at the time of introduction of TPDS. Additional allocations requested by States 
are made at APL rates. States/UTs have been authorised to lift rice and wheat against 
APL/additional allocation at APL rates i.e., 100% of the economic cost or open market 
sale price which ever is lower provided that it will not be less than levy price of rice for 
the State. Further, from December, 2000 onwards allocation of foodgrains for BPL 
families has been revised as per the number of BPL families on the basis of projected 
population of Registrar General as on 1.3. 2000 instead of earlier population base of 
1995.

mainstrcaming of children into formal schools within a maximum period of 3 
years. So far 96 NCLPs have'been sanctioned in 13 child labour endemic states 
for the rehabilitation of about 2.00 la kh children withdrawn from work. Under 
the Scheme of Grants-in-Aid, funds are released to Voluntary Organisations, on 
the recommendation of the concerned State Governments, for taking up action 
oriented projects for the benefit of working children. Over 50 projects are under 
implementation under the scheme.

Shortage of employment generation 
2192. SHRI ANANTRAY DEVSHANKER  DAVE: Will the Minister of 
LABOUR be pleased to state: 
(a) whether employment in the Central Government has been declining in the 
country; 
(b) whether Government, Banks and other Public Sector Undertakings are 
encouraging voluntary retirements; 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(d) the reasons as to why the retirement age was made 60 years when there is acute 
shortage of employment generation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR (SHRI MUNI LALL): 
(a) no, Sir. 
(b) and (c) Government Rules provides for seeking retirement by a Government 
Servant after completion of 20 years qualifying service by giving notice of not less than 
3 months in writing to the Appointing Authority. This option is purely voluntary which 
is available to Central Government Servant. 
Banks have been advised to carryout detailed manpower planning in order to adopt 
measures to have optimum human resources at various levels in keeping with the business 
strategies and requirement of each bank. Accordingly, out of the 19 nationalised banks, 
18 banks have introduced the Voluntary Retirement Scheme. 19th Bank viz.. Corporation 
Bank has taken a decision not to introduce the scheme because they feel they have just 
adequate manpower and fairly good age profile. In addition, the scheme has also been 
introduced by State Bank of India and seve n of its Associate Banks. Some Central 
Public Sector undertakings are also implementing the Voluntary Retirement Schemes. 
(b) Unemployment aspect was taken into  consideration while increasing the age 
of Central Government Employees. It was observed that according to the 
130 

[15 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
Study Team commissioned by the Fifth Pay Commission, the average annual retirement 
during the period 1991 -94 were 1,10,000. The annual retirement were of the order of 
94,605,1,46,951 and 90,643 for 1993-94, 1992- 93 and 1991-92 respectively. This 
means that even if Group "D' staff who retire at the age of 60 years are exluded, the 
increase in retirement age is likely to benefit 90,000 persons in Group A, B and C and 
around 55,000persons in the Armed Forces. There may not be any direct correlation 
between this and the filling up of conseque ntial vacancies in Government. This is 
because, as on date, around three lakh posts are vacant in the Central Government due to 
the built-in delays in recruitment, or candidates declining to join within specified period, 
or dropping out later; adequate v acancies would, therefore, be available to fill up the 
posts which are considered functionally necessary. In practice, in several areas, the 
vacancies being filled up today relate to what have occurred a few years ago. This being 
so, a certain level of recruitment process would invariably continue notwithstanding 
any increase in the age of retirement. Further, roughly one-third of the employees of the 
Central Government already retired at the age of 60 years and, therefore, vacancies in 
these cadres would continue to be available for fresh recruitment, further reducing the 
impact on unemployment. That apart with the opening of telecom, civil aviation, 
petroleum, roads and power sectors to private entrepreneurs, a lot of technical personnel 
are leaving Government in large numbers to  join the private companies. The telecom 
sector is on the verge of manifold increase in the field of both cellular and basic services 
and in both these areas employment opportuni ties will be generated in the private 
sector. Similarly, in the civil aviation sector, the air taxi operators have since been given 
the status of scheduled airlines and are accordingly poised for expansion. In respect of 
power and petroleum sector new projects are coming up and MNCs and joint venture 
companies are attracting technical personnel from ONGC, Oil India, NTPC, NHPC, 
BHEL and incresae in the age of superannuation would, to some extent, arrest the dramatic 
attrition which is taking place from public sector undertakings to private sector 
companies. The process of privatisation on the civil side is taking place in context of long-
term structural changes in the economy and would have the twin effect of reducing non-
plan expenditure and creating employment oportunities in private sector. To that 
extent, any impact on employme nt situation due to increase in the retirement age is 
expected to be offset by creation of new jobs in the private sector. In the case of Armed 
Forces, the nature of warfare is changing in  favour of less labour intensive but more 
capital-intensive warfare.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR (SHRI MUNI 
LALL): (a) to (c) Review/updation of La bour Laws is a continuous process and 
amendments/fresh legislations are made depending on the results of the review. A large 
number of labour laws have been framed over a period of time to address a number of 
issues and problems that assumed importance and attracted peinted attention at a 
particular point of time. The process of liberalisation, economic reforms and structural 
adjustment was set in motion in 1991. This  was followed by changes in the fiscal 
regime, trade policy, foreign and investment policy and restructuring of Public Sector. 
The main objectives of all these changes was to make the Indian industry more 
competitive. As most of the labour legislations were enacted long time back these 
require certain changes. In order to ensure both consistency of labour laws with the 
general changes taking place in  the economic policy and to provide for health, safety 
and welfare of the working class, the Second National Commission on Labour has been 
set up as per resolution issued on 15.10.1999 which will dispassionately look into 
these aspects and suggest appropriate changes in the labour legislation/labour policy.

Disruption of Dhama Organised by Bhartiya Bhasha Andolan 
2205. SHRIJANESHWAR MISHRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Dharna organised by the organisation named 
'Bhartiya Bhasha Andolan' in support of their demand to allow the official language as a 
medium of examinations conducted by UPSC has been disrupted recently; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefore; and 
(c) what action is being taken by Govern ment to implement the Parliamentary 
Resolution on Official Language? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND 
TRAINING AND DEPARTMENT OF PENSIONS AND PENSIONERS WELFARE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBL IC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS 
(SHRIMATIVASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) and (b) Some activists under the banner of Akhil 
Bhartiya Bhasha Samrakshan Sangthan were sitting on dharna in a shamiyana adjacent 
to the main entrance of UPSC since long. Keeping in view the sensitive nature of work 
of the Commission, the competent authoriti es removed the temporary structure on 
16.2.2001. 
(c) The official Language resolution,  1968 passed by both the Houses of 
Parliament had the following two components:— 
(i) that compulsory knowledge of either Hindi or English shall be required at the 
stage of selection of candidates for recruitment to the Union services or posts 
except in respect of any special services or posts for which a higher standard 
of knowledge of English alone or Hindi alone, or both, as the case may be, is 
considered essential for the satisfactory performance of the duties of any such 
service or post; and 
145 
 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2001] 
(ii) that all the languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution and 
English shall be permitted as alternative media for the All India and higher 
Central Services examinations after ascertaining the views of the Union Public 
Service Commission on the future scheme of the examinations, the 
procedural aspects and the timing. 
So far as component (i) of the Resolution is concerned, the same stands 
implemented so far as selection of candida tes through examinations held by UPSC is 
concerned. As regards component (ii) of the Resolution, the same has been implemented 
in respect of the Civil Services (Main) Examination held by Union Public Service 
Commission. However, so far as its' extension to other examinations held by the UPSC is 
concerned, there is no consensus amongst the St ate Governments/UTs etc. in this regard. 
Union Public Service Commission also feels that this will not only compromise with the 
confidentiality and impartiality of the examination process but will also have practical 
problems in implementation.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISIN-
VESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN  THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING. 
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF 
STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND 
PUBLIC GRIEVANCRS OF THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE): (a) The Planning 
Commission estimates the percentage of persons living below the poverty line at 
national and state level from the large sa mple surveys on consumer expenditure 
conducted by the National Sample Survey Organization (NSSO) at an interval of 
approximately five years. These percenta ges are applied on the estimated population 
in order to arrive at the number of poor in  the country. The two latest such surveys 
were conducted in 1993-94 (NSS 50th Round) and 1999-2000 (NSS 55th Round). The 
number of persons l i v i n g  below the poverty line calculated fr om 50lh Round large 
sample survey on consumer expenditure conducted by the NSSO in 1993-94 was 
320.4 million, which is 35.97 per cent of the total population. The data from the latest

living below the poverty line in the country in 1999-2000 as 260.25 million, which is

166 

[15 March, 2001] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) and (c) No lime frame has been fixed by the Government for total elimination 
of poverty. However, the Ninth Five Year Pl an has projected the percentage of people 
living below the poverty line to less than 5% by the end of the perspective period (2011-
12). 
There is a three-pronged action to alleviate and reduce the poverty in the country. 
These are: (i) acceleration of economic grow th, (ii) human, and social development 
through literacy, education, health, nutrition, meeting of the minimum needs, elevation 
of social and economic status of the weaker sections of the society, etc., and (iii) direct 
attack on poverty through employment and income generating programmes and assets-
building for the poor. 
The incresc in income of the people living below the poverty line occur from the 
joint impact of general growth process and direct income generation of the poor arising 
from various anti-poverty programmes introduced from time to time by the Government for 
their upliftment. Since the Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85). the Government has been 
implementing employment and asset generation schemes for the upliftment of the 
people living below the poverty line. These schemes are mainly of two types, sell-
employment and wage employment. Integrated Rural Development Programme 
(IRDP) has been the major self-employment programme and it has been in operation in 
all the blocks of the country since 1980. The wage employment programme initially 
was National Rural Employment Programme.(NREP) during the Sixth Plan period. In the 
Seventh Plan, another wage employment programme under the name Rural Labour 
Employment Guarantee Programme (RLEGP) was introduced. Then in 1989, Jawahar 
Rozgar Yojana(JRY) was launched by merging the National Rural Employment Programme 
and the Rural Labour Employment Guarantee Programme, and it became the main wage-
employment programme. In addition, several programmes to help the poor were also in 
operation until March, 1999. These programmes are:Million Wells Scheme (MWS), 
Employment Assurance Scheme (EAS), Development of Women and Children in 
Rural Areas (DWCRA), Training of Rural Youth for Self-Employment (TRYSEM), 
Supply of Improved Toolkits to Rural Artisans (SITRA). 
From 1st April, 1999, these programmes, excepting EAS and JRY have been 
restructured into single self-employment programme called the Swarnajayanti Gram 
Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) with the primary objectives of 
167 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2001] 
focusscd approach to poverty alleviation, capitalising advantages of group le nd in g, 
and overcoming the problems associated with mu l ti p l i ci ty  of programmes. Also, from 
1st April, 1999, Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY) has been restructured as Jawahar Gram 
Samridhi Yojana (JGSY) with the primary objective of creation of demand driven 
community village infrastructure including durable assets at the village level and assets to 
enable the rural poor to increase the opportunities for sustained employment. Its 
secondary objective is generation of supplementary employment for the unemployed 
poor in the rural areas. The wage employment under the programme is given to Below 
Poverty Lines (BPL) families. 
From 1.12.1997, Swarna Jayanti Sahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) is the main poverty 
alleviation programme in the urban areas.  The SJSRY, which has subsumed all the 
earlier three urban poverty alleviation programmes, viz., Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY), 
Urban Basic Services for the Poor (UBSP), Prime Minister's Integrated Urban Poverty 
Eradication Programme (PM1UPEP), seeks to provide gainful employment to 
unemployed or underemployed urban and educated up to IX standard for setting up self 
employment ventures or provision of wage employment. The implementation of SJSRY 
is relying on suitable community structures on the UBSP pattern and delivery of inputs 
under this programme is through the medium of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) and such 
community structure.

INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that as a result of liberalisation and globalization during

(b) whether it is also a fact that goods and material of every kind is being dumped 
illegally; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) the steps being taken by Government to protect Indian industries; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE 
INDUSTRIES AND AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES (SHRIMATI 
VASUNDHARA RAJE): (a) to (c) The small-scale sector as a whole has been exposed

(d) and (e) The threat of injury to domestic products is being addressed through 
anti-dumping action, imposition of countervailing duties and safeguard measures under 
the relevant WTO agreements. 
The Designated Authority appointed by the Government of India for 
conducting Anti-Dumping investigations in  India has till date recom- mended 
imposition of anti dumping duties in 60 cases, preliminary duty in 16 cases and 10 cases 
are under investigation. The Government has also issued notification requiring 
compliance of all the conditions of the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged 
Commodities) Order 1977 on imports as appli cable to domestic producers. Importers 
of 131 products shall be required to register themselves with Bureau of India Standards

constituted to assess the impact of remova l of quantitative restrictions and suggest 
suitable corrective measures.

and Tiny Sector was announced on 30th August, 2000 to strengthen the small scale 
sector and enhance its competitiveness both domestically and globally. The policy package 
inter-alia includes easier access to credit availability of collateral free composite loans 
upto Rs. 25 lakhs, capital subsidy for technological upgradation and improved 
infrastructure.

Establishment of International Criminal Court 
1. DR. MAHESH CHANDRA SHARMA: W ill the Minister of EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government agree w i t h  the proposal to establish an International 
Criminal Court; 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether Government are aware of any appeal made by any NGO for 
ratification of the Statute of the International Criminal Court; and 
(d) if so, the details of such an appeal and Government's response in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI J ASWANT SINGH): (a) to (d) 
Government have not singned the Statute of the International Criminal Court. 
There are several deficiencies in the Statute including that it brings under the 
purview of the Court several crimes which are subject to national jurisdiction, and makes 
the primacy of national jurisdiction subject to satisfaction of the Court; it does not 
include terrorism as a crime against humanity. It Mso gives special and discriminatory 
powers to the UN Security Council to refer to. or block consideration by, the Court, of 
cases. 
191 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2001] 
Government are awre of appeals by NGOs and others for ratification of the Statute 
of the International Criminal Court. In view of continued validity of concerns relating to 
several of the provisions in, and omissions from, the Statute of the International Criminal 
Court, there is no change in Government's position.
